correctness.rationale: At E_y the candidate tangent (1,−B/(p−a)) must be an eigenvector of the axial derivative, giving d(p−a)(a+cB)=Bp and the unique p=a+X. For U=a+x+cy, V=dx+y, clearing denominators gives UV H(T(x,y))=x[(p/X)V−dU]=ad x H. Its positive cofactor makes the nonnegative segment invariant and preserves the sign off the segment. There the reciprocal coordinate 1/x−1/X is multiplied by λ⁻¹; the two-sided explicit orbit therefore connects E_x to E_y. The known global-basin theorem is applied correctly: p/(a+cB)=λ<1 and B/(dX)=λ⁻¹>1, giving precisely the strict E_y branch. At E_y the spectral radius is λ, so an equivalent local contraction norm gives O(θⁿ) errors for any λ<θ<1. The positive normalized x recurrence has 1+O(θⁿ) multipliers, yielding A>0, and the defect cofactor divided by κAλⁿ also has a convergent positive product. Multiplying gives λ^{n(n−1)/2}, with signed finite nonzero C_H for H_0≠0. The defect is o(x_n), so the orthogonal projection has x-coordinate x_n+O(H_n) in (0,X) eventually, verifying the actual distance-to-segment limit. Exactly on the segment no log-distance is asserted.
residual_risks: No rate away from the exact resonance is established. The n² law concerns transverse distance, not distance to E_y or convergence of points on the axes.

value.rationale: The natural geometry is the two given competitive-exclusion equilibria and the question of when their connecting segment is exactly invariant. The cofactor reveals spatial approach to that segment at an n² logarithmic scale for every off-segment positive orbit even though its axial coordinate decays geometrically. That distinction is quantitative information missing from a known qualitative global limit or local zero eigenvalue.
residual_risks: The exact orbit formula is only on a codimension-one resonance and only on the segment; it does not solve arbitrary trajectories globally.
